name: gfx_texture
doc: Where a texture's content is, one instance per live texture (src/gfx/texcontent.ts). WebAssembly cannot protect pages, so CPU writes to texture storage are not seen as they happen (nxnative nvn_dirty.c); the state is checked when a submission first needs the texture. Unknown: the host texture holds nothing the recorder vouches for; its first use uploads the storage (deswizzled). Uploaded carries the sampled hash of the storage it was uploaded from: at the first use in each later submission the sampled hash is taken again (and the full hash when the range was flushed, or periodically within a budget), and a difference is Stale: uploaded again. GpuOwned: a render pass, a copy or a clear wrote it; guest memory no longer describes it and it is never uploaded again. Staged: texels were written into the storage by a command or call (CopyBufferToTexture, WriteTexels) while the storage owned the content: the next use uploads, and a GPU write that keeps the old content (a pass that loads, a partial copy) uploads first. Lost is the GPU device being lost: what was uploaded is uploaded again from the storage; a GpuOwned texture's content is gone and stays GpuOwned (it is drawn again or stays empty). CpuWrite is the one way out of GpuOwned, only with the game profile's tex_flush_upload (src/gfx/texwatch.ts): the game flushed a pool range over the storage and the storage is no longer what it was when the GPU took the texture, so the CPU published new content: Unknown, and the next use uploads it.
